edit.description: The kitchen-sink corpus's two hooks re-spell onto handlers: `sessionHook` (:132, a one-line flat `hook({ name, type, command })`) and `auditHook` (:141, the `http` handler carrying its `url`). The surrounding comment (:135-:140) is stale at HEAD already and rides this edit — it says `hook`'s "per-handler-kind `when` guards fire on the member's own `type`", but the six guards moved to `handlerDefaultContract` (`sdk/src/builtins.ts`:1952) and bind under `handler` alone (:2032); `hookDefaultContract` (:2038) is now the event enum alone. What the cell exercises is unchanged — a guard composing over a group-array registration beside the object-shape and scalar-shape ones — but it now composes over the handler child, and the comment must say so.

Both Rust string-fixture programs author the same flat `sessionStart` hook — `SETTINGS_MEMBER_PROGRAM` (:39, the 0050 container posture) and `SETTINGS_RESIDUE_PROGRAM` (:61, the pre-0050 contrast). The hook is scaffolding in both (the cell is about which member governs `.claude/settings.json` whole), so the re-spell is mechanical; the arms' member tallies move if a handler child now counts.

The fourth program, found at the 839589ee..HEAD audit and missing from this entry's first census: `gate_installed_does_not_report_superseded_by_member` (:1684) writes an author's own `.temper/hooks/SessionStart.ts` as a Rust string (:1715-:1723) spelling `hook({ name, type: "command", command })` flat. Re-spell it onto `hooks: [{ type, command }]`. Behavior-preserving: supersession keys on the member owning the event, not on the handler spelling, and the flat residue reaches the same projected group through `json_manifest::hook_matcher_group`'s residue arm either way. The two scaffolded-module assertions in this file already read the array grain (:1287-:1298, :1427-:1433, moved there by c9a73aec), so the fixture is the one site left disagreeing with its own file.

The shipped example — the most adopter-visible copy of the refused spelling, and the reason this entry is not merely fixture hygiene: `hook_sessionStart` (:8) and `hook_guard` (:16) both author the flat triple, and the file's own header calls them "fields-only registration members". Re-emit the example's lock after the re-spell: `examples/*/.temper/lock.toml` is a standing build surface in chain.ts, so it needs no declaration, and `tests/it/emit.rs`'s own failure message spells the recipe — `ln -s $PWD/sdk examples/base-harness/.temper/node_modules/@dtmd/temper` (gitignored, never committed), then `cargo run -- emit --into examples/base-harness/.temper` and commit what moves.

Two claims about the authoring surface are false at HEAD and ride this entry — the corpus re-spell is what makes them legible. `hook_matcher_group`'s doc (:727-:730) says the flat-residue arm is "what the SDK's `hook()` authors today — the surface HOOK-AUTHORS-ITS-HANDLERS moves onto the array — and until it moves, both spellings reach this one face"; `hook()` authors the array (`sdk/src/builtins.ts`:556) and `Hook` types no handler key at all (:485, `hooks: readonly Handler[]`, required). The unit test's comment at :1166 repeats the same forward reference. Restate both as the standing rule the arm carries — a group-array member whose fields spell a handler flat, carrying no member-array key, nests into the one handler it means — with no pointer at shipped work. The arm itself stays: it is generic over any group-array kind's `member_key`, its own unit test (:1163-:1188) keeps it non-vacuous after the three fixtures re-spell, and dropping residue silently (or refusing it) is intent the corpus body does not carry.

summary: Every authored hook in the corpus spells its handlers — the four in-fence programs still authoring the flat field triple the SDK's types no longer accept.

tests.asserts: the corpus's `check`/`emit` snapshots re-baseline with the two hooks' handler children in the member tally, and the `http` handler's guard still fires where it now binds
`emit_program_runs_the_shipped_example_harness` stays green — the re-spelled example program links, and its re-emitted `lock.toml` byte-matches the committed one
`gate_installed_does_not_report_superseded_by_member` stays green on the re-spelled fixture — the authored group still supersedes temper's gate hook at its event

acceptance: cargo test green, `pnpm --dir sdk test` green, clippy/fmt clean, and a PCRE2 `rg` for a `hook({` call passing `type`/`command`/`url`/`timeout` before any `hooks:` key (`--hidden`, so `.temper/` trees are in scope) finds only the one file named in notes.
notes: The staleness half of the HOOK-AUTHORS fence capture, kept narrow so the hook spine's head stays small: all four programs are GREEN on the flat spelling today (node type-strips them; the write face nests residue into one handler), so this is a corpus authoring a shape its own types refuse, not breakage. Fifth site, outside every build fence: `.temper/hooks.ts`:18,25,37,45 — the dogfood's own, a human `chore(harness):` commit. scoped at 152fed1a
